aspects.says: A sorted set treats its comparator's 0 as a duplicate, so a collator at PRIMARY strength drops names that differ only in case or accents.
basis: section:compareTo Orders UTF-16 Units; People Need a Collator, and Its 0 Merges Set Entries

aspects.says: compareTo orders by UTF-16 unit, so capitals come before lowercase and accented capitals after z; CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER fixes case only; a Collator for an explicit locale orders for people.
basis: section:compareTo Orders UTF-16 Units; People Need a Collator, and Its 0 Merges Set Entries

aspects.says: toLowerCase() uses the default locale, so a case-insensitive key built with it breaks under a Turkish default, while equalsIgnoreCase and toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) do not.
basis: section:equalsIgnoreCase Has No Matching hashCode: Compare and Hash One Key

aspects.says: String.equals is true only for another String with the same units, so a StringBuilder with the same text is never equal, Objects.equals included; contentEquals compares any CharSequence.
basis: section:equals Is True Only for Another String, and Its Receiver Must Not Be null

aspects.says: A hash set or map looks by hashCode before it asks equals, so an equals that ignores case beside a hash of the raw text lets case variants in.
basis: section:equalsIgnoreCase Has No Matching hashCode: Compare and Hash One Key

aspects.says: The same text can arrive as different code points (é as U+00E9 or e + U+0301); equals and hashCode differ until both are normalized to one form such as NFC.
basis: section:Text That Looks the Same Can Be Different Code Points: Normalize Before Comparing

aspects.says: x.equals(y) throws when x is null while equals(null) is false; Objects.equals treats two nulls as equal.
basis: section:equals Is True Only for Another String, and Its Receiver Must Not Be null

aspects.says: Objects.equals adds null-safety only and calls the same equals, so it does not compare a String with a StringBuilder by content.
basis: section:equals Is True Only for Another String, and Its Receiver Must Not Be null

aspects.says: equals and hashCode must use one canonical key, because equalsIgnoreCase's per-code-point fold and toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) disagree on letters such as the dotless i.
basis: section:equalsIgnoreCase Has No Matching hashCode: Compare and Hash One Key

aspects.says: Removing accents is not normalizing: it merges different words such as René and Rene.
basis: section:Text That Looks the Same Can Be Different Code Points: Normalize Before Comparing
